source_text: Εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ὑπέμεινεν ὁ κύριος παραδοῦναι τὴν σάρκα εἰς καταφθοράν, ἵνα τῇ ἀφέσει τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἁγνισθῶμεν, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ αἵματι τοῦ ῥαντίσματος αὐτοῦ. γέγραπται γὰρ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἅ μὲν πρὸς τὸν Ἰσραήλ, ἃ δὲ πρὸς ἡμᾶς, λέγει δὲ οὕτως: Ἐτραυματίσθη διὰ τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν καὶ μεμαλάκισται διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν: τῷ μώλωπι αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν: ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἄφωνος ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος αὐτόν. οὐκοῦν ὑπερευχαριστεῖν ὀφείλομεν τῷ κυρίῳ, ὅτι καὶ τὰ παρεληλυθότα ἡμῖν ἐγνώρισεν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἐνεστῶσιν ἡμᾶς ἐσόφισεν. καὶ εἰς τὰ μέλλοντα οὐκ ἐσμὲν ἀσύνετοι. λέγει δὲ ἡ γραφή: Οὐκ ἀδίκως ἐκτείνεται δίκτυα πτερωτοῖς. τοῦτο λέγει, ὅτι δικαίως ἀπολεῖται ἄνθρωπος, ὃς ἔχων ὁδοῦ δικαιοσύνης γνῶσιν ἑαυτὸν εἰς ὁδὸν σκότους ἀποσυνέχει. ἔτι δὲ καὶ τοῦτο, ἀδελφοί μου: εἰ ὁ κύριος ὑπέμεινεν παθεῖν περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς ἡμῶν, ὢν παντὸς τοῦ κόσμου κύριος ᾧ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου: Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ’ εἰκόνα καὶ καθ̓ ὁμοίωσιν ἡμετέραν: πῶς οὖν ὑπέμεινεν ὑπὸ χειρὸς ἀνθρώπων παθεῖν; μάθετε. οἱ προφῆται, ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἔχοντες τὴν χάριν, εἰς αὐτὸν ἐπροφήτευσαν: αὐτὸς δέ, ἵνα καταργήσῃ τὸν θάνατον καὶ τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν δείξῃ, ὅτι ὲν σαρκὶ ἕδει αὐτὸν φανερωθῆναι, ὑπέμεινεν, ἵνα τοῖς πατράσιν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν ἀποδῷ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἑαυτῷ τὸν λαὸν τὸν καινὸν ἑτοιμάζων ἐπιδείξῃ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὤν, ὅτι τὴν ἀνάστασιν αὐτὸς ποιήσας κρινεῖ. πέρας γέ τοι διδάσκων τὸν Ἰσραὴλ καὶ τηλικαῦτα τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα ποιῶν ἐκήρυσσεν, καὶ ὑπερηγάπησεν αὐτόν. ὅτε δὲ τοὺς ἰδίους ἀποστόλους τοὺς μέλλοντας κηρύσσειν τὸ εὐαγγέλιον αὐτοῦ ἐξελέξατο, ὄντας ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν ἁμαρτίαν ἀνομωτέρους, ἵνα δείξῃ, ὅτι οὐκ ἦλθεν καλέσαι δικαίους, ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς, τότε ἐφανέρωσεν ἑαυτὸν εἶναι υἱὸν θεοῦ. εἰ γὰρ μὴ ἦλθεν ἐν σαρκί, οὐδ’ ἄν πως οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἐσώθησαν βλέποντες αὐτόν, ὅτε τὸν μέλλοντα μὴ εἶναι ἥλιον, ἔργου τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχοντα, ἐμβλέποντες οὐκ ἰσχύουσιν εἰς τὰς ἀκτῖνας αὐτοῦ ἀντοφθαλμῆσαι: οὐκοῦν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τοῦτο ἐν σαρκὶ ἦλθεν, ἵνα τὸ τέλειον τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἀνακεφαλαιώσῃ τοῖς διώξασιν ἐν θανάτῳ τοὺς προφήτας αὐτοῦ. οὐκοῦν εἰς τοῦτο ὑπέμεινεν. λέγει γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τὴν πληγὴν τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἐξ αὐτῶν: Ὅταν πατάξωσιν τὸν ποιμένα ἑαυτῶν, τότε ἀπολεῖται τὰ πρόβατα τῆς ποίμνης. αὐτὸς δὲ ἠθέλησεν οὕτω παθεῖν: ἔδει γάρ, ἵνα ἐπὶ ξύλου πάθῃ. λέγει γὰρ ὁ προφητεύων ἐπ’ αὐτῷ. Φεῖσαί μου τῆς ψυχῆς ἀπὸ ῥομφαίας, καί: Καθήλωσόν μου τὰς σάρκας, ὅτι πονηρευομένων συναγωγαὶ ἐπανέστησάν νέστησάν μοι. καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Ἰδού, τέθεικά μου τὸν νῶτον εἰς μάστιγας, τὰς δὲ σιαγόνας εἰς ῥαπίσματα. τὸ δὲ πρόσωπόν μου ἔθηκα ὡς στερεὰν πέτραν.
pass_a_gloss: For to this end the Lord endured to deliver his flesh to destruction, so that by the forgiveness of sins we may be purified, which is in the blood of his sprinkling. For it is written concerning him, some things to Israel, and some to us, and it says thus: He was wounded for our transgressions and bruised for our sins: by his stripe we were healed: as a sheep he was led to slaughter, and as a lamb silent before the one shearing him. Therefore we ought to be very thankful to the Lord, because he also made known to us the things that have passed and in the present things he has made us wise. And we are not without understanding concerning the things to come. And the scripture says: The nets are not spread in vain for the winged creatures. This it says, that justly a man will perish, who having the knowledge of the way of righteousness turns himself to the way of darkness. And yet, my brothers, if the Lord endured to suffer for our soul, being the Lord of all the world, to whom God said from the foundation of the world: Let us make man according to our image and likeness: how then did he endure to suffer at the hands of men? Learn. The prophets, having the gift from him, prophesied concerning him: and he, so that he might abolish death and show the resurrection from the dead, because it was necessary for him to be revealed in the flesh, endured, so that to the fathers he might give the promise, and he himself, preparing for himself a new people, might show on the earth, being, that he, having made the resurrection, will judge. For teaching the end to Israel and doing such great signs and wonders, he preached and loved him exceedingly. But when he chose his own apostles, who were going to preach his gospel, being more lawless than all sin, so that he might show that he did not come to call the righteous, but sinners, then he revealed himself to be the Son of God. For if he had not come in the flesh, men would not have been saved by seeing him, when they cannot even look at the sun, which is a work of his hands, because they are not able to gaze at its rays: therefore the Son of God came in the flesh for this purpose, so that he might sum up the perfect things concerning sins for those who persecuted his prophets to death. Therefore he endured for this purpose. For God says the stroke of his flesh is from them: When they strike their own shepherd, then the sheep of the flock will be destroyed. But he himself willed to suffer thus: for it was necessary for him to suffer on the wood. For the one prophesying concerning him says: Spare my soul from the sword, and: Pierce my flesh, because the assemblies of the wicked have risen up against me. And again he says: Behold, I have set my back for scourges, my cheeks for slaps. And I have set my face as a hard rock.

bible_refs.note: He was wounded for our transgressions
As a sheep he was led to slaughter

pass_b_english:
The Lord endured the surrender of his flesh to corruption for this very purpose: that through the forgiveness of sins we might be cleansed — a cleansing that comes through the blood of his sprinkling (Isaiah 53:5). Scripture bears witness to him, addressing some things to Israel and others to us, and it says: “He was wounded for our transgressions and bruised for our sins; by his stripe we were healed. Like a sheep he was led to the slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer” (Isaiah 53:5, 7). Therefore we owe the Lord immense gratitude, because he has revealed to us the past and made us wise in the present, and we are not without understanding about the future. Scripture also says: “The net is not spread in vain for the birds” — meaning that a person justly perishes who, having known the way of righteousness, turns himself onto the way of darkness. 

And yet, my brothers, consider: if the Lord endured suffering for our soul, though he is Lord of all the world — the one to whom God said at the foundation of the world, “Let us make man in our image and likeness” — how did he come to endure suffering at human hands? Learn this: the prophets, possessing the gift from him, prophesied about him. He himself endured, so that he might abolish death and demonstrate the resurrection from the dead; for it was necessary that he be revealed in the flesh. He did this to fulfill the promise to the fathers and, while preparing a new people for himself, to show on earth that he, having brought about the resurrection, will judge. He taught Israel to the very end, performing such great signs and wonders, and he loved them exceedingly. 

But when he chose his own apostles — those who would proclaim his gospel — they were men more lawless than any other sinners, so that he might prove he came not to call the righteous but sinners. Then he revealed himself as the Son of God. For if he had not come in the flesh, human beings would not have been saved by seeing him; they cannot even gaze at the sun, a work of his own hands, because they cannot endure its rays. Therefore the Son of God came in the flesh for this very reason: to bring to its climax the complete dealing with sins on behalf of those who persecuted his prophets to death. That is why he endured. 

God declares that the stroke upon his flesh comes from them: “When they strike their shepherd, then the sheep of the flock will be destroyed.” Yet he himself willed to suffer in this way, for it was necessary that he suffer on the wood. The prophet speaking of him says: “Spare my soul from the sword,” and “Pierce my flesh,” for the assemblies of the wicked have risen against me (Psalm 22:16). And again: “Behold, I have given my back to scourges and my cheeks to slaps; I have set my face like a flinty rock.”

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text. Pass A provides a literal rendering, while Pass B provides a more fluent version with appropriate scripture citations (Isaiah 53:5, 53:7, and Psalm 22:16) that match the quoted content. The translation of 'ὑπερευχαριστεῖν' as 'very thankful' (A) and 'immense gratitude' (B) correctly handles the intensive prefix. The translation of 'ἀνακεφαλαιώσῃ' as 'sum up' (A) and 'bring to its climax' (B) is faithful to the sense of the Greek.
